affectedSurfaces: progress-reviewer citation validation and action materialization
hypothesis: Projecting the reviewer's AgentDef write scope into every filesystem-capable harness, while separately granting only an isolated per-run agent-output directory and digest-binding runtime-authored evidence before agent execution, prevents a compromised reviewer from modifying workflow evidence or authorizing actions with evidence forged after collection without breaking required workflow finish artifacts.

metricsCompared.name: forged evidence actions materialized
metricsCompared.baseline: A reviewer could rewrite progress-review-evidence.json, cite only the forged ID, and pass both citation validation and apply-actions authorization.
metricsCompared.candidate: 0 tasks and 0 owner questions are created after the fake harness rewrites the evidence artifact and cites only its forged ID; the digest mismatch fails before apply-actions.
metricsCompared.unit: unauthorized materialized actions in the regression fixture

metricsCompared.name: reviewer writable runtime authority
metricsCompared.baseline: Native and Claude-capable reviewer launches could receive a whole-workspace write root while the declared AgentDef write scope was checked only against Git-visible post-step mutations.
metricsCompared.candidate: Native CLI, Claude SDK, and KOTA-hosted tool paths enforce deny-all reviewer project scope plus one per-run agent-output descendant before filesystem mutation; Claude's effective canUseTool path rejects sibling runtime state even under a wider scope policy or after an earlier callback rewrites the target.

metricsCompared.name: focused progress-reviewer regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: No runtime workflow test exercised post-collection evidence forgery across the reviewer agent boundary.
metricsCompared.candidate: Repair attempt 7 passes 157 tests across 26 progress-reviewer, Claude, cross-harness, hosted-tool, workflow, and strict-types files with 1 platform-gated skip; repository lint (3,509 files), type checking, build, and task validation pass.
metricsCompared.unit: passing focused tests and static checks

rationale: The candidate closes a confirmed high-severity reviewer authority gap at two independent boundaries: AgentDef.writeScope is now a pre-mutation filesystem authority enforced by native CLI sandboxes, Claude's effective SDK canUseTool path plus command sandbox, and KOTA-hosted tools, and every authoritative evidence reread must match the pre-agent SHA-256 digest. A separate per-run agent-output capability preserves mandatory workflow rationale and commit artifacts without exposing sibling runtime state, including when the canonical run directory is outside a task worktree. The runtime regression deliberately forges the evidence artifact and proves fail-closed behavior before side effects; cross-harness, workflow, and strict-types tests prove only the isolated output descendant remains writable. The output exception bypasses only the project-path catalog and still subjects destructive calls to owner confirmation, so no authorization, approval, tool-risk, sensitive-data handling, or injection-defense control is weakened.
